answer: PoA prices identity by accumulated judgment rather than by a key. Each epoch an address must answer a rotating challenge in its own words, and peers grade it; only answers that survive jury review raise standing. A sybil farm therefore has to spend the same continuous, parallel, verifiable reasoning per clone, and clones that share one voice are flagged as a hollow echo. Reputation lives on addresses whose history held up, so a new batch of keys lands on barren shale rather than a haven of trust. The attacker's cost is not one deployment but months of graded work per alias.
